title: fix(console): FormPage degrades an unregistered widget to the type renderer (objectui#10472)
body:
Fixes #10472

## What changed

`FormPage`'s `resolveFieldWidgetKey` took an authored `widget` whenever one was present and returned `resolveFormWidgetType(widget)`. That resolver answers a spelling nothing registers with the `text` widget, so a `select` field carrying an unknown `widget` rendered a free-text input. The spec's `FieldSchema.widget` describe (installed `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0`, read verbatim; its placeholder is spelled WIDGET here because GitHub strips angle-bracket fragments): "Form widget override — names a registered field component (resolved as `field:WIDGET`) to render this field instead of the `type` default. Degrades to the `type` renderer when unregistered."

The `widget` leg now runs only when `namesRegisteredWidget(widget)` holds. Otherwise the row falls through to the arity leg and the `type` leg of the same resolver.

- Files: `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` (+44 / -6), new `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.widgetDegrade-10472.test.tsx` (+135), new `.changeset/10472-formpage-widget-degrades-to-type.md` (+19, `@object-ui/console` patch).
- No list of widgets was added. The lookup (H2) is `resolveFormWidgetType` itself, which is the same call the leg already made and the resolver whose loaders `getLazyFieldWidget` mounts. It is read for its documented unknown answer ("anything unknown falls back to `text`"): a spelling answered with `text` that is not itself `text` named nothing. A registered key, a retired spelling (its tombstone) and an alias the resolver knows keep resolving as before.

## Premise check (H1–H4)

- H1 confirmed on `origin/main` `111fa4c`. The widget leg was `if (field.widget) return resolveFormWidgetType(field.widget);`.
- Before, measured at `111fa4c` with real widgets on `/forms/:name`: `{ type: 'select', options, widget: 'no_such_widget' }` rendered `INPUT[type=text]`. `{ type: 'boolean', widget: 'no_such_widget' }` rendered `INPUT[type=text]`.
- After, measured at `735c9ed` with the same probe: the select field renders `BUTTON[role=combobox]` plus the hidden `SELECT`. The boolean field renders `BUTTON[role=switch]`. `{ type: 'password', widget: 'no_such_widget' }` renders `INPUT[type=password]`. `{ type: 'select', multiple: true, widget: 'no_such_widget' }` renders the multiselect group.
- Controls in the same run: `widget: 'radio'` on a select renders `radiogroup`. `widget: 'owner'` renders the tombstone. `widget: 'secret'` on a text field renders `INPUT[type=password]`. `widget: 'json'` on a text field renders the code widget's `TEXTAREA`.
- H3, the record form (`packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx`), was measured with the dev's probe shape and real widgets after `registerAllFields()`. It shows the same symptom, and **it is not changed here**. `select` / `field:select` with `widget: 'no_such_widget'`, and a metadata-carried `field.widget: 'no_such_widget'`, all render `INPUT[type=text]`. `field:boolean` with the same widget renders `INPUT[type=text]` too.
- Why form.tsx is a different mechanism: an unregistered spelling there reaches the ruled "unregistered-widget default" branch (objectui#5322 / objectui#5375). That branch reads the spelling. Measured at `735c9ed`: `{ type: 'field:text', widget: 'secret' }` and `{ type: 'field:text', widget: 'ui:password' }` both render `INPUT[type=password]`.
- A plain degrade-to-type there would hand those rows to the registered text widget. How the spec's degrade rule composes with that secret ruling is a decision, so it is reported as a finding, not guessed here.
- A fix in form.tsx would also have to converge three precedence sites: `resolveWidgetType` (boolean seeding), the cascade-clear effect's own `widget || type`, and the render `resolvedType`. It would also have to update the core validator's `resolveAuthoredFieldWidgetId`, which says it mirrors that precedence.
- H4: the `field:`-qualified spellings are not ones the shared resolver knows, so after this PR they degrade to the type in `FormPage`. Measured at `735c9ed`:
  - `widget: 'field:owner'` on a `user` field renders the person picker (`lookup-trigger`), with no refusal. Before this PR it rendered a working `INPUT[type=text]`, also with no refusal.
  - `widget: 'field:textarea'` renders `TEXTAREA` on a `textarea` field and `INPUT[type=text]` on a `text` field.
- The record form resolves both `field:`-qualified spellings as registry keys: the tombstone for `field:owner`, and `TEXTAREA` for `field:textarea` on a text field.
- The bare retired `widget: 'owner'` still reaches the tombstone in `FormPage`, and that is pinned here. That the tombstone names the row's live `type` (`data-retired-field-type="user"`) is objectui#10471, left as is. Whether a `field:`-qualified spelling is authorable on a form view at all was not measured here (the card lists it as unmeasured).

## Ablation (fix committed first, mutated through `ablation-replace.mjs`, restored to HEAD with an empty `git diff HEAD`)

1. The guard was reverted to `if (field.widget) {`. Result: 2 failed | 2 passed (4). The two degrade pins went red and both controls stayed green.
2. `namesRegisteredWidget` was made to always answer false. Result: 2 failed | 2 passed (4). The registered-`radio` control and the retired-`owner` control went red, and the degrade pins stayed green.

## Acceptance notes

- The pending `.changeset/10179-formpage-shared-field-resolver.md` says "An authored `widget` wins over `type`". After this PR that holds only for a widget that names something registered. This PR's changeset states the refinement, and both publish in the same release. That body was not edited because it is outside the claimed file surface.
- `FormPage` still resolves alias spellings in `widget` (`json` renders code, `secret` renders password), while the record form treats them as unregistered (`json` renders `INPUT[type=text]`). Both were measured above. That difference existed before this PR and is recorded here, not decided.
